title: Provenance-completeness linter + run-manifest validator (CI gate)
context: The reproducibility standard requires that 100% of published quantitative assertions carry a resolvable run-manifest entry. Without an automated CI gate, this guarantee is aspirational. The provenance-completeness linter and manifest validator close this gap: the build fails if any published assertion lacks provenance, if the manifest schema is violated, or if floating container tags or missing checksums/versions are found. Golden fixtures must use synthetic/tiny public spectra — never patient-derived raw data — so CI never ships restricted material.
objective: Implement the provenance-completeness linter and run-manifest validator as a CI gate that fails the build on any provenance gap, manifest schema violation, floating container tag, or missing checksum/version.
acceptanceCriteria: CI fails the build if any published assertion (over the countable unit fixed in repro-standard-003) lacks a resolvable run-manifest entry.

The manifest validator rejects run manifests that violate the schema defined in repro-standard-003: missing fields, floating container tags (no sha256: digest), missing input/output checksums, or missing tool/DB versions.
Golden test fixtures use only synthetic or tiny public spectra (no patient-derived raw data); fixtures are committed to the repo.
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass; commit is DCO signed-off; code is MIT-licensed.
resources: PLAN.md — Solution approach, Provenance binding section
output: A committed provenance-completeness linter and run-manifest validator integrated as a CI gate, with synthetic golden fixtures and passing pnpm build/test/lint.
